findings.class: Input-domain gap: partial decoding of git's C-quoted paths
findings.scenario: git C-quotes the porcelain path and, because core.quotePath defaults to true, writes each non-ASCII byte as an octal escape. I reproduced this with real git. A Lighthouse profile folder `C:\Users\José\lighthouse.80415070` with `Local State` inside shows up as `?? "C:\\Users\\Jos\303\251\\lighthouse.80415070/Local State"`. The unquote only collapses `\\`, so `\303\251` stays literal. The regex still matches the name, but `Path(worktree, folder, "Local State").is_file()` checks a folder that doesn't exist and returns False. worktree_blockers then reports `1 uncommitted change(s)`, so the merged worktree is held for review, which is the behavior the bug report asks to fix. The same mis-decoding hits `!!` entries going through regenerable(). It fails safe (the worktree is held, nothing is deleted), but the fix doesn't work for any Windows profile path with a non-ASCII user name.
findings.fix: Decode git's quoting fully. One way is to unescape the C string to bytes, e.g. `codecs.escape_decode(path[1:-1].encode())[0].decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape')`. A simpler way is to run the status call in worktree_blockers with `-c core.quotePath=false`, or use `-z` and drop unquoting. Add a test with a non-ASCII user folder.

A detached worktree has branch "", so prs.get("") is None and it is never listed as held after merge, and the same goes for a no-PR branch inside the default branch. It also says nothing about auto/apply now deleting untracked Lighthouse Chrome-profile folders (the shutil.rmtree in execute()) before `git worktree remove`.
findings.fix: Remove the "(or that is detached inside the default branch)" clause so the text says only a merged PR's branch or worktree is listed. Add one line saying that an untracked root-level `lighthouse.NNNNNNNN` folder holding a Chrome profile's `Local State` counts as build output and is deleted along with the worktree.
